_meta.b68_changes: FOUR CORRECTIONS HE CAUGHT IN THE TURN LABELLER, and one of them is a rename. (1) CHAIR 3 LINE DOES NOT RUN INTO LOOK MA — a mislabel, and every line carrying it is gone: one chain, 'Windows Road (top of 4/5/11) → Chair 3 Line → Look Ma', route 11 on the tops of #4, #5 and #11 into Mid-Vail, 6 edges. Removed by a NEW mechanism, ROUTEKILL, gated by route_kill_v: CARDDROP takes a whole card and DEDUPE's drop list needs an exact via, so neither could reach one bad pair sitting in the middle of a chain. (2) BWANA LOOP TURNS LEFT ONTO BORN FREE (LOWER) and carries on straight, it never meets Born Free (bottom) directly. (3) SAFARI (BOTTOM) RUNS INTO SIMBA (BOTTOM), which then feeds Born Free (bottom). (4) WINDOWS ROAD ENDS AT HUNKY DORY, which is what feeds you to Chair 3 Line — same turn signal, merge right, and the road ends there. Those three are VIAEDIT v6 inserts rather than swaps, so every pair either side of an insert is one his label set already holds and nothing new needs labelling. THE RENAME: KLICKITY KLACK (LOWER) IS NOW CHAIR 6 LINE, his call, reversing the 2026-08-31 note that said naming it for the lift line would be useless. THE ID MOVES WITH IT — klickity_klack_lower → chair_6_line, his call, 'not having another Silk Road moment': an id that disagrees with its name is the split that cost a day on Silk Road and again on Minnie's. The old id had exactly one home, the dictionary line — it is in no export, no screen, not plan.html and not the labeller — so nothing is left pointing at a dead id, and RUN_MIGRATE carries it regardless the way every id rename since windows_road has been carried. VIARENAME v6 carries the NAME through 144 chain positions in saved data. FOUR TURN LABELS MOVE WITH IT and have to be re-seeded when the labeller is rebuilt off a B68 export: Klickity Klack → Chair 6 Line (was straight), Chair 6 Line → Skid Road (bottom) (merge left), Skid Road (bottom) → Chair 6 Line (left), Chair 6 Line → Brisk Walk (merge left). Route count drops by 3 stored cards’ worth of one route each; nothing else changes. ONE MORE, FROM A FULL RUN-NAME AUDIT OF THE WHOLE GRAPH: an HTML-escaped ampersand was baked into nine via chains in the BAKED fallback — ‘Steep & Deep’ on six and ‘Coyote’s Escape & Den’ on three — naming two runs the dictionary does not hold. His saved graph is clean, so it only ever reached a fresh device. BAKED is corrected in place and VIAEDIT v7 is the net. The audit found nothing else: no other orphan name, no arrow inside a run name, no curly/straight apostrophe split, no run following itself, no blank chain segment, and every name in every chain resolves to a difficulty. TWO MORE IDS CORRECTED. front_step → first_step. The run is First Step; front_step was a typo rather than a decision, and it is on p14’s seed runs list and in no saved data, so RUN_MIGRATE covers the one place it could have landed. AND CHAOS CANYON WAS ONE RUN WEARING TWO IDS, chaos_canyon and chaos_canyon_kaz — the second took a suffix at B48 because the first was already in the dictionary when the eleven Kids Adventure Zones went in, and kaz is Kids Adventure Zone. Vail has one Chaos Canyon, off Lion’s Way below Mid-Vail. Collapsed to chaos_canyon, which matches the name; RUN_MIGRATE carries the suffixed id and BAKED is rewritten. The stale copy was also sitting on #4’s seed runs list, which was wrong on its face — it is a Mid-Vail-level run and Hayden put it on #1 himself — so it comes off #4 and NEWRUNS v16 keeps it on #1. His saved graph had it on no pod at all, so nothing he has typed moves.
_meta.b67_changes: AVANTI PARK GETS ITS TWINS. Every line in the graph that finished on Avanti (bottom) now has a second card with → Avanti Park → Avanti (bottom) as its tail, so dropping through the park is something the user picks rather than a detour the graph hides. 38 edges ended that way; 32 cards went in at route_add_v 3, because the other six were already exact duplicates of each other in the saved graph and applyRouteAdd collapses them on the via match. The single leg off the top of Black Forest #27 is excluded on Hayden’s call: it joins Avanti below the park, so a twin would be a route nobody can ski. TIMES ARE THE PARENT’S AND ARE NOT RIGHT YET — a park lap is slower than skiing past it, by however long you spend on the features, and a TIMEFIX matched on these vias is how to set them. B67b, same day: the twins now carry the parent’s time PLUS ONE MINUTE, his call — a lap through a park costs about a minute of features. Set at source in ROUTEADD v:3 and carried to anyone who already took them at the old time by TIMEFIX v:3, guarded on `was` so a hand-retimed card is left alone. THE SIX DUPLICATE CARDS ARE GONE, by a new versioned applyDedupe at dedupe_v 1: sameness is mode, via and minutes, and the survivor keeps the union of both segment lists, because one copy of each pair carried j9|t|p2 and the other carried none. rSig would have called them different and left all six. The 159 repeated BLANK route rows are deliberately untouched — an empty slot is scratch space, not a route. The Avanti (mid) → Avanti (mid) double-type needed nothing: VIAEDIT v1 already clears it on load, and it only survives in the stale BAKED snapshot. B67c, same day: PICKEROON (bottom) HAS THREE EXITS, NOT ONE. His call — it finishes where Upper Lion’s Way, Avanti Park and Avanti (bottom) all meet, and merges right onto the two Avanti runs. The graph only knew Upper Lion’s Way, so all ten routes through it had a single ending and the turn label he gave for the park had no route to attach to. Each of the ten keeps its line and gains two at route_add_v 4: the same stem onto Avanti (bottom) at the parent’s time, and through the park at parent plus one. The Upper Lion’s Way tail is dropped from the new pair, not extended — three ways out of one spot, not one after another. B67d: his B67 export came back with the double-typed Avanti (mid) alive in two of the Avanti Park twins. ROUTEADD copies a via exactly as written and BAKED still carried the double, and applyViaEdit only ever runs from applyExport, so VIAEDIT v1 had never reached his saved data. Both twins are corrected at source and the same find/replace is re-issued as VIAEDIT v3 so it lands in a browser loading off saved work. DEDUPE goes to v2 behind it, because collapsing the double makes those two identical to routes already on their cards. The export now writes dedupe_v, which it did not, so the version survives a round trip instead of resetting to zero on every import. B67e: AVANTI PARK IS NOT A RUN OFF THE TOP OF #2, his call. It is out of p2’s runs_off_top in the PODS array, and NEWRUNS v36 is withdrawn by RUNDROP v37 — a new array that shares runSeedV with NEWRUNS and does the one thing the seeder could never do, take a run back off a pod. It needed to exist because v36 had already shipped and been saved, and pulling the id out of PODS only ever reaches a browser with no saved work. You reach the park off Avanti (mid), Upper Lion’s Way, Cookshack or Pickeroon (bottom), every one of them below the summit, so it sits mid-chain like Wildcard and Cookshack, which are in no pod’s list either. The 42 routes through it are untouched: a via names a run, it does not require that run to hang off a top.

The VIAFIX split renamed it in the via text long ago and the graph uses 'Windows Road (top of 3/7/17)' and 'Windows Road (top of 4/5/11)' sixty times between them, but the DICTIONARY never got the split and still carried the unsplit parent, so neither half had a difficulty of its own and the lengths tool had neither name at all. _meta.b63_changes: NO RUN NAME CONTAINS AN ARROW ANY MORE. Silk Road (21 → base of 22) becomes SILK ROAD (SIBERIA BOWL) and Silk Road (top of 22 → bottom) becomes SILK ROAD (MONGOLIA BOWL), real key renames to silk_road_siberia and silk_road_mongolia. The arrow is the chain separator, so a name containing one was ambiguous to everything that reads a chain: 'Silk Road (21 → base of 22) → Poppyfields' read as THREE runs, and the turn labeller was offering 'Silk Road (21' as a run to label, with turn buttons under a run that does not exist. 37 route chains were affected. VIARENAME is now TWO PASSES: raw entries are matched against the whole via string FIRST, longest name first so one can never eat another, and only then is the chain split on arrows and matched segment by segment. Verified: zero old silk names left, zero ghost segments, and zero run names anywhere still carrying an arrow.
_meta.b62_changes: SEVEN LOCATION NAMES BECOME RUN NAMES, real key renames. _meta.b58_changes: A VIA TEXT correction, and a new one-time mechanism to carry it: VIAEDIT, gated by via_edit_v the same way every other fix is gated. Avanti (mid) was typed twice in one chain off the top of #2, so three edges read Pika \u2192 Avanti (mid) \u2192 Avanti (mid) \u2192 Chair 2 Line. That produced a run-to-run transition from a run to itself, which the turn labeller can never offer a row for, so it was the one gap in the label set that was not a beginner carpet. VIAFIX could not express the edit \u2014 its guard skips any via that already contains the target text \u2014 which is why the mechanism is new rather than another VIAFIX entry.
_meta.b57_changes: The three route times he ruled on after the suspect-times pass: the Log Chute path (Northface Catwalk (top) → Log Chute) 5 → 4 off both the top of #6 and the bottom of #11, Blue Ox 11 → 9, and Poppyfields West → Poppyfields 6 → 5 on all three cards (top of #14, top of #24, and the top of #21 chain that carries China Bowl to Two Elk in front of it — China Bowl to Two Elk itself is unchanged, the 6 was the whole chain). Shipped as TIMEFIX v1, a one-time versioned fix, because a route's minutes live in saved user data and editing the seed or BAKED alone never reaches a browser that already has work in it. It matches on the card AND the exact via chain, checks the old value before writing so a later hand edit is never overwritten, and ships with an empty TIMEUNDO list from the start. _meta.segment_semantics: A segment reference means EVERY path from its from-node to its to-node, including multi-hop paths through other nodes, not only the routes stored in that one card. Nodes that are physically the same spot (welds, summit groups, base clusters) are treated as one node. Composed depth is capped at 40 legs; counting assumes a downhill graph. Same-spot legs are arrival-only: they can end a path, never continue one.
